correctness.rationale: For all \(m\ge2\) and \(0<t\le1\), the Lipschitz ball dissects into 2m congruent minimum-coordinate chambers; each is an interval [0,t] times m-1 independent square bands |u-v|<=t. Explicit band difference and midpoint moments determine both covariance eigenspaces via the pair-swap/permutation action. Their rational formulas are equal to those independently checked in five exact weighted-Ehrhart configurations. Algebra factors the eigenvalue gap into strictly positive terms for \(t<1\); the smallest spectral projector U has negative -1/2 entries exactly on the matching. A monotone truncated-difference second moment identifies t. Direct substitution covers \(t=1\) and limits cover fixed-t and boundary-layer asymptotics. The finite checks support but do not prove the all-m result.

value.rationale: The second moment of uniform Lipschitz potentials is a natural quantitative descriptor of a finite-metric Banach dual ball. The theorem converts it into an inverse recovery mechanism for the labeled metric matching, provides an exact spectral separation with a sharp near-equilateral scale, and locates the precisely nonidentifiable boundary. It distinguishes covariance information from volume, facet, projection and distortion data for a continuous all-dimensional family, giving a mathematically motivated classification.
